title: 306 Men Vanished Without a Trace — Then Two More Ships Did the Same
description:
On March 4th, 1918, the USS Cyclops left Barbados carrying 306 men and 10,800 tons of manganese ore. It was already dangerously overloaded, yet Captain George Worley — a German-born officer once accused by his own crew of being a spy — took on even more cargo instead of unloading. The ship was due in Baltimore nine days later. It never arrived. No SOS. No wreckage. No lifeboats. The Navy searched a million square miles and found not a single plank or body. President Wilson said only God and the sea knew what happened.

But here's the part nobody talks about: twenty-three years later, two sister ships — same class, same manganese route — vanished too. Same silence. Same nothing. Three ships. One pattern. Zero answers, then or now.
